Yes — NovaLearn should fund and prioritize the Advanced OCR Pipeline before accelerating the Microsoft Teams integration.

- **Current support demand:** Scanned PDF processing is the primary driver of citation errors and customer onboarding delays [NL-001-S08]. In May, 27% of support tickets were related to import issues and broken citations from scanned PDFs, and the support queue is clogged [NL-015-S06]. The OCR fix is viewed as a “critical system stability requirement,” not a nice-to-have, because without it the platform is unreliable for compliance-heavy clients [NL-015-S06].

- **Onboarding impact:** Scanned PDFs remain the primary onboarding bottleneck [NL-016-S01]. The Advanced OCR Pipeline, scheduled for August 2026, is meant to automate document validation and citation mapping, directly reducing this bottleneck [NL-001-S08][NL-032-S05]. If Teams is accelerated before OCR, NovaLearn risks delivering inaccurate, un-cited answers to a larger audience inside a chat app [NL-015-S06].

- **Roadmap status:** The official roadmap has Advanced OCR as the highest technical priority for August 2026 [NL-001-S08][NL-015-S06]. Teams is only “in design / planned for Q4 2026” and not generally available [NL-014-S01][NL-023-S04]. Internally, the Teams connector is still an early proof-of-concept lacking security controls and tenant isolation [NL-023-S04]. Rushing it would require a full auth-layer redesign and create a tenant-isolation and security-certification risk [NL-015-S06].

Although Teams is the most common feature request and customers are asking for an accelerated timeline [NL-011-S07], the support and onboarding strain from OCR problems is the more immediate operational constraint. The correct sequencing is to keep OCR as the funded August priority and keep Teams on its planned Q4 design and early 2027 development path [NL-015-S06].
